_about: Field terms for F147, same shape as papers/glossary.json.

dqe.definition: the share of the information carried by the arriving photons that a detector's output keeps, measured as the square of its output signal-to-noise ratio divided by the square of the input's; 1 is a perfect photon counter
dqe.excludes: the plain share of photons absorbed, and the speed of a film

neq.definition: the number of photons a perfect detector would need to give the same signal-to-noise ratio as the real output
neq.excludes: the number of photons that arrived

characteristic-curve.field: photographic sensitometry; also called the H and D curve
characteristic-curve.definition: the developed optical density of a film plotted against the logarithm of the exposure it received
characteristic-curve.excludes: the film's spectral sensitivity and its grain

net-density.definition: optical density above the film's base and fog, so that unexposed film reads zero
net-density.excludes: the density of the base and the fog themselves

gamma.definition: the local slope of the characteristic curve: the change in density per unit change in log exposure
gamma.excludes: the display gamma of video and computer screens

granularity.definition: the standard deviation of density read through a small round aperture scanned across a uniformly exposed patch; Kodak's sheets use a 48 micrometre aperture
granularity.excludes: how grainy the image looks to a viewer, and noise measured at other apertures

spectral-sensitivity.definition: for each wavelength, the reciprocal of the exposure energy per unit area needed to reach a stated net density, here 0.2
spectral-sensitivity.excludes: sensitivity to white light or to a named illuminant

siedentopf-rule.definition: the classic statement that the variance of density grows in proportion to the mean density, so that rms granularity grows as its square root
siedentopf-rule.excludes: Selwyn's law, which concerns the size of the measuring aperture

hold-out.definition: the error of a model fitted on one part of the data and scored on a part it never saw; here fitted on the lowest 70 percent of the axis and scored on the top 30 percent
hold-out.excludes: an error computed on the points used to fit

bic.definition: a model score that adds a penalty for each fitted parameter to the misfit, lower being better, so that a more flexible model must earn its extra parameters

hinge-form.definition: a response that is zero below a threshold exposure and rises in a straight line above it, here in log exposure
hinge-form.excludes: any form that saturates at high exposure

poisson-threshold.definition: a model in which each grain, or each rod cell, responds once it has absorbed at least n photons, with photon counts following Poisson statistics; n is the hit number
poisson-threshold.excludes: models in which response grows smoothly with every photon

benjamini-hochberg.definition: a rule for many tests at once: rank the p values from smallest, and reject the k smallest when the kth is no larger than k over the number of tests times the chosen false discovery rate, here 0.05
benjamini-hochberg.excludes: a correction for one test, and the stricter Bonferroni rule
